summary:
[  edit  ]
The Point Transform  TOP  treats the RGB values of the input image as a point cloud of XYZ positions or vectors and performs 3D transformations and alignments. When the input type is set to 'Vector', translations are ignored and only rotation and scaling operations are performed. The alpha channel, if present, is passed along to the output image unchanged.
Transformations can be defined directly on the Transform page, taken from an input  CHOP  (see  Transform CHOP ), using the Look At parameter, or as a combination of any of those methods.
The Align page allows you to move or scale the point cloud relative to the origin, a 1x1x1 cube, or to a reference object. For example, you can scale the cloud to fit inside another point cloud or piece of geometry, or you can align the point cloud to sit on the XZ plane, or directly beside another cloud.
The second input can optionally be used as a weight map to control how much of the transformation is applied to each individual point.

inputs.description: points  - The first input contains the position data of the points represented in the red, green, and blue channels.,

weights  - The second input contains an optional weight map that controls how much of the transformation is applied to each point. The weight channel and weight range parameters control how the color channels of the image are converted into weights.

parameters.label: Input Type
parameters.name: inputtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose if the RGB channels of the input texture should be treated as positions or vectors. Vectors will not have the translation portion of the transform applied to them, and can be normalized before and/or after the transformation is applied.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.name: position
parameters.description: The RGB values represent XYZ positions.

parameters.label: Vector
parameters.name: vector
parameters.description: The RGB values represent XYZ directions.

parameters.label: Normalize Input
parameters.name: innormalize
parameters.description: RGB input vectors are rescaled to a length of one before they are transformed.

parameters.label: Normalize Output
parameters.name: outnormalize
parameters.description: RGB vectors are rescaled to a length of one after they are transformed.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Changes the order that the translate, rotate and scale operations are performed on the input. Analogous to how you would end up in different locations if you were to move a block and turn east, versus turning east and then moving a block.  In matrix math terms, if we use the 'multiply vector on the right' (column vector) convention, a transform order of Scale, Rotate, Translate would be written as T * R * S * Position

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - As with transform order (above), changing the order in which the rotations take place will alter the final position and orientation. A Rotation order of Rx Ry Rz would create the final rotation matrix as follows R = Rz * Ry * Rx

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - Move the input positions in the X, Y and Z axes. If the input is set to 'Vector', the translate values will have no effect.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - Rotate the input RGB values around the corresponding X, Y and Z axes. Angles are given in degrees.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - Scale the input RGB values in the corresponding X, Y and Z axes. If 'Normalize Output' is on, then all output values will be rescaled to a length of one regardless of the scale values.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - The pivot is the point about which the input points or vectors are scaled and rotated. Altering the pivot point produces different results depending on the transformation performed on the object.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Scale the input values along all axes simultaneously.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.name: invert
parameters.description: Invert the transformation i.e. preform the reverse movements.

parameters.label: Look At
parameters.name: lookat
parameters.description: Allows you to orient your input points by naming the object you would like them to Look At, or point to. Once you have designated this object to look at, it will continue to face that object, even if you move it.

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.name: upvector
parameters.description: ⊞  - When orienting an object towards the 'Look At' target, the Up Vector is used to determine where the positive Y axis points.

parameters.label: Forward Direction
parameters.name: forwarddir
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets which axis and direction is considered the forward direction.

parameters.label: Transform  CHOP
parameters.name: chopinput
parameters.description: Path  to a  CHOP  node with channels describing a 3D transformation. These channels may come from a  Transform CHOP  or another  CHOP  with the correct channels defined.

parameters.label: Multiply Order
parameters.name: multiplyorder
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls whether the transformation from the given  CHOP  is applied to the input values before or after the transformation describe by this node.

parameters.label: Weight  Channel
parameters.name: weightchannel
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select how to use the colors of the second input image as weights for transforming the points of the first input.

parameters.label: Weight Range
parameters.name: weightrange
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the range of weight values used to control how much of the transformation is applied to a point. Points with the minimum weight will  not  be transformed, while points with the maximum weight will be  fully  transformed. A linear interpolation is applied to points with weights that fall between the minimum and maximum.

parameters.label: Align Transform Order
parameters.name: alignxformorder
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines the order that align operations are performed on the input points.  Note : Unlike Scaling on the transform page, the alignment scale is always done relative to the center of the point cloud so that the point cloud's center does not change.

parameters.label: Reference   Node
parameters.name: alignref
parameters.description: A path to a  TOP  or  SOP  node used to align the input points after the transformation.  Note  Using another point cloud  TOP  as a reference will incur additional performance costs because of the need to calculate the dimensions of the reference points.

parameters.label: Align Operation Order
parameters.name: alignopord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the order in which scale and transform is applied when aligning.

parameters.label: Align Scale
parameters.name: alignscale
parameters.description: ⊞  - The Align Scale can be used to resize the point cloud to fit inside the given bounds. Scaling can be done per axis (maintaining proportions or stretching), or on all axes.

parameters.label: Per Axis
parameters.name: peraxis
parameters.description: Scaling is controlled separately per-axis using the parameters below.  Note:  It is possible to have conflicting scales when setting limits on multiple axes.

parameters.label: Unity
parameters.name: unity
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized to fit within a 1x1x1 cube. Proportions are maintained so that the largest dimension will have a length of 1.

parameters.label: Reference
parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized to fit within the dimensions of the reference object. Proportions are maintained.

parameters.label: Align Scale X
parameters.name: alignscalex
parameters.description: ⊞  - The point cloud is resized based on its width in the X axis.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: No scaling is done based on the X axis.

parameters.label: Unity
parameters.name: unity
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized along the X axis so that the total width is 1. This does not affect the other axes and will distort the overall shape of the cloud.

parameters.label: Reference  Input
parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized along the X axis to the width of the reference object. This does not affect the other axes and will distort the overall shape of the cloud.

parameters.label: Unity Proportional
parameters.name: unityprop
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized so that the total width in the X axis is 1. Other axes are scaled accordingly to maintain proportions.

parameters.label: Reference  Proportional
parameters.name: referenceprop
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized to match the width of the reference object. Other axes are scaled accordingly to maintain proportions.

parameters.label: Align Scale Y
parameters.name: alignscaley
parameters.description: ⊞  - The point cloud is resized based on its height in the Y axis.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: No scaling is done based on the Y axis.

parameters.label: Unity
parameters.name: unity
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized along the Y axis so that the total height is 1. This does not affect the other axes and will distort the overall shape of the cloud.

parameters.label: Reference  Input
parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized along the Y axis to the height of the reference object. This does not affect the other axes and will distort the overall shape of the cloud.

parameters.label: Unity Proportional
parameters.name: unityprop
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized so that the total height in the Y axis is 1. Other axes are scaled accordingly to maintain proportions.

parameters.label: Reference  Proportional
parameters.name: referenceprop
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized to match the height of the reference object. Other axes are scaled accordingly to maintain proportions.

parameters.label: Align Scale Z
parameters.name: alignscalez
parameters.description: ⊞  - The point cloud is resized based on its depth in the Z axis.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: No scaling is done based on the Z axis.

parameters.label: Unity
parameters.name: unity
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized along the Z axis so that the total depth is 1. This does not affect the other axes and will distort the overall shape of the cloud.

parameters.label: Reference  Input
parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized along the Z axis to the depth of the reference object. This does not affect the other axes and will distort the overall shape of the cloud.

parameters.label: Unity Proportional
parameters.name: unityprop
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized so that the total depth in the Z axis is 1. Other axes are scaled accordingly to maintain proportions.

parameters.label: Reference  Proportional
parameters.name: referenceprop
parameters.description: The point cloud is resized to match the depth of the reference object. Other axes are scaled accordingly to maintain proportions.

parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution.

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Fits the width and height to the resolution given below, while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The width and height are limited to the resolution given below. If one of the dimensions exceeds the given resolution, the width and height will be reduced to fit inside the given limits while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Enables the  Resolution  parameter below, giving direct control over width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height

parameters.label: Fit Best

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside

parameters.label: Native  Resolution

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. Making this larger than 1 is essentially the same as taking the output from each pass, and passing it into the first input of the node and repeating the process. Other inputs and parameters remain the same for each pass.
